item.title: Barstool’s Joke about Raiders QB Goes Viral
item.description: Sep 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) reacts after the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Some people just know how to tap into what fans feel without trying too hard. That is exactly what happened when a Barstool Sports personality compared rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza to a lost love. The comment aired during an episode of the “Big Boys Club” earlier this week and struck a nerve with everyone who watched Indiana win the national title. The clip has now racked up over 1.2 million views in just two days, proving that nostalgia sells better than any highlight reel. Ella Grif did not hold back on her feelings about the Raiders’ rookie. She told the show’s hosts that she feels sad because the young quarterback reminds her of a perfect past relationship that is gone forever. “I’m sad because Fernando feels like the ex-boyfriend that was so perfect that you’ll never get back. And you just look back on it, you compare everything to him,” Grif said. That simple line explains why so many Hoosiers fans are already looking for a way to watch Mendoza play, even though he is now wearing a silver-and-black jersey. The Natty That Never Was The sadness Grif talked about comes from a specific moment in time that can never be repeated. Indiana fans know that winning the championship this year felt different because of the player at the helm. Even if the team wins every single game left on the schedule, the feeling will not match what they had with Mendoza. “And also, even if we went undefeated this year… Even if it was the same thing and we went to the Natty, it wouldn’t feel the same… That makes me sad,” she added. The emotional weight of that loss is real, and it makes the transition to the pros harder for the fans than the player. This viral moment does more than just make people laugh; it changes the timeline for the Raiders. The team has lost four straight games after starting 3-0, and the pressure is mounting on Kirk Cousins to turn things around. With a 23-year-old talent waiting in the wings, the question is no longer if Mendoza will start, but when he will get the keys to the offense. According to the New York Post , the emotional impact he had on his former supporters will only increase Raiders fans’ desire to see his return to the field soon. A New Start in Vegas While fans argue about the past, the present situation in Las Vegas demands a change. The Raiders need a spark, and the rookie from Indiana seems ready to provide it.

item.title: Oscar Piastri: McLaren handled Mexico altitude “better than I was expecting”
item.description: Motorsport photo McLaren driver Oscar Piastri walks away from FP2 in Mexico City's circuit with optimism as he confirms his car coped better with the high altitude than he expected it to. This comes despite the driver having a "pretty messy" qualifying simulation. The Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez circuit sits more than 2,200 metres above sea level. The thin air leaves teams running with very little downforce and poor cooling, making it one of the most challenging weekends of the calendar. Speaking after FP2, Piastri said the conditions had not been as tricky as he had feared. “It was difficult for sure, but I don’t think necessarily worse than what I was expecting, or if anything it was probably a little bit better than I was expecting. So yeah, everything felt OK. I think we seemed to be relatively competitive, to be honest.” The Australian admitted his soft-tyre lap failed to come together, but believed the papaya-coloured team's underlying pace is strong. “My soft lap in FP2 was pretty messy, but I felt like the kind of overall pace seems to be there. So Ferrari looked very strong, which I guess you would kind of expect on a track like this, but I think we had a pretty good day.” Piastri said that cleaning up his mistakes should put him much higher up the order, but warned that beating Ferrari would be difficult. “There was a couple of very big mistakes, so I’m optimistic that if I can tidy those up, I’ll be a lot further up as well, which is a nice feeling to have. So I think to try and beat Ferrari tomorrow is going to be very tough, as it looks like. And it’s very tight, I would say, through the whole field, so you’re going to have to be on top of the game.” Oscar Piastri, McLaren Oscar Piastri, McLaren Asked how he had adapted his driving to the conditions, Piastri said the low grip was nothing new under this year’s regulations. “It’s tough. It’s just incredibly low grip. I think with this year’s cars, honestly, it’s a similar story in most places, so it doesn’t feel that dramatic here. But it’s always a challenge, not just for the car in terms of balance, but cooling the engines this year, it’s always very tough.” Mercedes driver George Russell suggested on Thursday that Ferrari’s smaller turbo could give it “quite an advantage” at altitude, with the 2026 rules having dropped the MGU-H that previously helped to eliminate turbo lag. But Piastri doesn't agree that the turbo will be the deciding factor, adding that Ferrari didn't look especially fast in a straight line. “They looked very quick today. I don’t think the turbo is going to make as much of a difference as we thought. They, if anything, looked a bit slow on the straights, so let’s wait and see tomorrow. Definitely in some circumstances it will help them, but I think in normal conditions it’s not as big of a factor as we first thought.” To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Sherrock upsets Littler to claim £501,000 prize
item.description: Fallon Sherrock won £25,000 for reaching the third round of the PDC World Championship in December 2019, but earned £501,000 on Friday [Getty Images] Fallon Sherrock defeated reigning world champion Luke Littler in one leg of darts on Friday to win £501,000. Broadcast live globally on Netflix, Beat Luke Littler featured a host of amateur players taking on world number one Littler in a one-leg face-off at Manchester Central. Players could not be members of the PDC Tour, meaning Sherrock, who became the first female player to beat a male opponent at the PDC World Championship on her way to the last 32 in December 2019, was allowed to compete. After Littler had defeated 14 amateurs, some as young as 14, he was always going to have a tough task against 32-year-old Sherrock, a player who has won 21 times on the Women's PDC Series. She had been closest to the bull to start first and hit a 180, only the third maximum of the night, before taking out double 20 to clinch the prize. Sherrock, whose son Rory was among the crowd, said: "It's insane, I can't put it into words of what it means, especially having Rory here - it's his first time at anything and he has seen me win. "It's a great moment and I will memorise this forever. Give me an opportunity and I will take it every time. I'm really proud of myself, I rise to the occasion." Nineteen-year-old Littler, who has won the PDC World Championship in both the past two events, said: "Brilliant, that's what one person had to do - win the bull and go out in 15 [darts] and that's what she did, world class." Darts with a difference The packed crowd in Manchester was in boisterous mood with many fans in fancy dress, but this was darts with a difference. There had been 25,000 applicants who had entered the competition. The first stage saw players have to get down from 501 in 24 darts or less, with those successful then facing a three-person interview panel, including 16-time world champion Phil Taylor, PDC president Barry Hearn and darts television pundit Laura Turner. Twenty players were due to play at the event. Sixteen were selected outright, while the eight most experienced players were paired off, with Netflix viewers voting on which one should be able to compete. Sherrock was in the vote against Germany's Jarod Becker, but picked up 75% of the votes to get the chance to face Littler. She had picked up £25,000 for reaching round three of the PDC World Championship at Alexandra Palace seven years ago after beating Ted Evetts and Mensur Suljovic before losing to Chris Dobey. Her achievement saw her nicknamed 'The Queen of the Palace' and she was also awarded an MBE for her services to darts in 2023. Sherrock's victory over Littler meant the event immediately ended, meaning the five remaining amateurs were unable to get their shot at the £501,000 prize. item.title: Villa to sue Carragher over 'unacceptable insults'
item.description: Jamie Carragher became a pundit following retirement from playing in 2013 [Getty Images] Aston Villa say they will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher over what the club branded as "unacceptable insults". Posting on their social media on Friday, Villa released a statement signed by their chairman Nassef Sawiris accusing Carragher of insulting the Premier League side and its fans. It added the club would "not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football". Speaking on the Stick to Football podcast, Carragher attracted criticism from Villa fans by suggesting their manager Unai Emery would be interested in becoming Manchester United's head coach. Michael Carrick's position at United is hanging in the balance after a dismal start to the campaign and Carragher said "Aston Villa will never be Manchester United". "Surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again," Carragher said. "There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not. "So Real Madrid will take Manchester United's best player, they did it with [Cristiano] Ronaldo. "And there will be teams below Aston Villa, and they'll take their players or manager, so shut the [expletive] up Aston Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Manchester United." Carragher, a football pundit for works for Sky Sports and American broadcaster CBS, has already commented on the backlash he received after he told the fans to shut up. "It was a joke after the stick Villa fans have given me over saying Emery may fancy joining Man Utd," Carragher said on social media. "I hope these clown clips show me praising Emery/Villa like I have done for years & saying how pleased I was you won [the 2026 Europa League] in Istanbul." On the Overlap Daily, Carragher went into more detail. "I just think Unai Emery is the best manager in the league and if you're Man Utd you're thinking 'what's the best we can get?'. I'm not saying he'll go - I'm just saying if it was me I'd ask the question," said Carragher. "Certain managers are good at certain clubs and that's Emery. He reminds me of Rafa [Benitez]. I think your own ego if someone said 'that's your level' would say 'no I'm not'. That was my point. "It's grew arms and legs. I ended up telling them to [expletive] which maybe I shouldn't have done but it was all in jest because they've been all over my social timeline. I was saying [expletive] off my socials." item.title: UIL reinstates Texas high school star QB Hayes Hackney ahead of regular-season finale
item.description: Argyle High School quarterback Hayes Hackney (2) throws a pass during the second half as Argyle High School hosted Lovejoy High School in a district 3-5A, Division II football game at Argyle ISD Stadium in Flower Mound on Friday night, October 9, 2026. (Stewart F. House/The Dallas Morning News) Texas high school quarterback Hayes Hackney is eligible to return after the University Interscholastic League overturned a district committee's ruling that had sidelined him over residency concerns. The UIL State Executive Committee voted 3-0 Thursday, Oct. 29, to restore Hackney's eligibility to play for Argyle High School, according to Texas HS Football . The decision reverses an Oct. 20 ruling by the District 3-5A Division II Executive Committee, which voted 6-0 that Hackney, a transfer from Prosper Walnut Grove, did not meet residency requirements. The dispute centered on whether Hackney's family lived within Argyle ISD boundaries while still owning a home in Prosper. During Thursday's hearing, the state committee found sufficient evidence that the family lives in Argyle. School administrators had testified that they made multiple home visits to verify the family's residence. State committee chairman Mike Motheral also questioned an earlier determination that Hackney had not transferred for athletic purposes. That issue was decided in May and was not part of Thursday's appeal. Hackney has thrown for 2,574 yards and 32 touchdowns with just two interceptions this season. Argyle is 8-1 and ranked No. 3 in Class 5A Division II. Argyle defeated Colleyville Heritage 45-35 last week with sophomore quarterback Cobe Wilson while Hackney was sidelined. Hackney can return Friday when Argyle faces Nevada Community in its regular-season finale ahead of the playoffs. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.description: Andrea Cambiaso: Man United join the race for Juventus ace as INEOS look to reinforce key position in January One area that Manchester United need to reinforce as early as possible is at left-back, where Michael Carrick is short on specialist options. Luke Shaw may have started every Premier League game last season, but the Englishman’s injury troubles have returned to haunt him. The 31-year-old has already missed seven games this season, leaving the head coach to utilise centre-back Ayden Heaven and right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui as stop-gap options on the left. Everyone knew it would be a risk not to sign a left-sided full-back in the summer, but the Red Devils’ single-minded focus on midfielders meant Lewis Hall remained at Newcastle . item.title: Bayern Munich’s Max Eberl talks Aaron Danks, Joshua Kimmich, and Der Klassiker
item.description: (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images With Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund level on points heading into Saturday’s Der Klassiker , Max Eberl knows just how important the showdown could be in shaping the Bundesliga title race. The Bayern sporting director expressed his respect for Dortmund’s development under Niko Kovač but made no secret of his ambitions for the match. “We’ve got a lot of respec t for Dortmund. We won in Dortmund last season, even though it was close. They were in good form as well last season and have continued that now. It’s Der Klassiker . They always challenge and push us. We want to win and create a lead over B VB. We’re currently equals in terms of the table,” said Eberl (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). Eberl was also asked about Aaron Danks stepping into the spotlight on the touchline amid the unexpected circumstances surrounding Vincent Kompany. He praised the collective effort o f the coaching staff and emphasized the importance of pulling together during a difficult period. “Things have happened that can’t be predicted. We have a coaching team that works together in an amazing way. We’re really grateful to have Aaron and the team. It’s not an easy situation. We’re working hard to come through all this a s a group. That’s how things have to be in football,” Eberl noted. Finally, Eberl addressed Joshua Kimmich’s personal situation following a fam ily bereavement. While the midfielder has returned to individual training and could potentially feature against Dortmund, Eberl made it clear that Bayern will not put any pressure on him to return before he is ready. “I’ve spoken with him. Life is diff erent for him now. When something like that happens in the family, life changes for you. We’ll give him all the support he ne eds. If Jo feels ready to get back involved, whether that could be tomorrow or not, he’ll decide that with the c oaching team. But we have to say that life is different for Jo now,” said Eberl. item.title: Leclerc quickest in Mexico GP practice
item.description: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc shows speed in Mexico (CARL DE SOUZA) Ferrari's Charles Leclerc dominated practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix on Friday, clocking the fastest times in both sessions for the second weekend running. The Monegasque driver clocked a best lap in one minute and 17.827 seconds in the second practice session to outpace McLaren's world champion Lando Norris by 0.103 seconds with George Russell finishing third ahead of his Mercedes team-mate runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli. Antonelli, 20, who was absent on Thursday to recover from a virus, can become the sport's youngest champion on Sunday, and Italy's first since 1963, if he finishes in the top nine. He can also take the title if his two remaining rivals – Russell and Ferrari's seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton – fail to win. Leclerc's success on Friday repeated his showing in Austin, Texas, at last weekend's United States Grand Prix. Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen, a record five-time winner in Mexico, was fifth ahead of team-mate Isack Hadjar after an early clash with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson which left him with damaged bodywork. Lawson's team-mate Arvid Lindblad was seventh ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly, Lawson and Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren. Seven-time champion Hamilton was down in 11th for Ferrari after suffering a power failure that ended his running midway through. The session began with Gasly leading Alpine team-mate Franco Colapinto out ahead of Cadillac’s local hero Sergio Perez, set for his 300th race start, the seventh driver to reach this landmark. He was promptly cautioned for a pit lane infringement. After the inclusion of 10 rookie reserves in free practice one, all 22 full-timers were back with a wide range of tyres on show – Ferrari taking mediums, Verstappen softs and others hards on the low-grip track. A red flag paused the action after 15 minutes to clear debris in the Foro Sol after Verstappen clashed with stable-mate Lawson and damaged his car’s bargeboard. The frustrated Dutchman's actions seemed excessively aggressive and required a Red Bull pit-stop for repairs. The incident was noted by the stewards and set for investigation afterwards. Ferrari dominated the early stages with Leclerc on top before Norris, on softs, took command as McLaren bounced back shortly before Hamilton lost power and pulled up on the straight. He had just switched to softs and completed one lap. It was a setback for Hamilton who lost vital learning time on softs while Leclerc regained the initiative ahead of Norris, Russell and Antonelli before the field switched to heavier fuel loads and medium tyres. str/rcw

item.title: Deeper Than Hate Rivalry On Halloween
item.description: Butch Dill-Imagn Images Two Sun Belt East rivals meet in Statesboro on a Saturday that doubles as Halloween . App State travels to Paulson Stadium for a 6:30 p.m. ET kickoff against Georgia Southern. This matchup matters more than a typical conference game because it decides who stays alive in the division race. Both teams need a win to keep their hopes for a title shot alive. The series carries a nickname that fans take seriously: “Deeper Than Hate.” That phrase was born from decades of hard hits and close scores, not just marketing fluff. History shows a tight split in the all-time record. App State leads the series 21-19-1 after 41 meetings, but the recent trend favors the Eagles. Georgia Southern has won the last three games and four of the last five contests. The most recent meeting ended on Dec. 29, 2025, in the Birmingham Bowl, where Georgia Southern crushed App State 29-10. That neutral-site game marked the first time the two programs met in a bowl since moving to FBS. OJ Arnold ran for 152 yards in that bowl win, proving the Eagles could dominate when it counted most. A Tale of Two Records App State enters this game with a 5-2 record and a 2-1 mark in the Sun Belt. The Mountaineers rode a high after beating previously unbeaten James Madison 34-31 in overtime on Oct. 22. James London kicked a 40-yard field goal to seal that win in front of a sold-out crowd in Boone. That victory put every team in the East Division at risk of losing the lead. Georgia Southern sits at 3-4 overall but holds a 2-1 record in conference play. Their win over Old Dominion on Oct. 15 snapped a four-game losing streak that looked ugly for a long time. The Eagles have played the exact same three league foes as App State this season. They beat Coastal Carolina 31-24 and Old Dominion 23-15 but lost at home to JMU 27-24. Their nonconference losses came against strong teams like Clemson and No. 18 Houston. Those tough losses mean their 3-4 record is misleading compared to their actual talent level. Per App State Athletics , the team is ready for a difficult challenge after avenging earlier losses to Coastal Carolina and JMU. The midweek victory against ODU was their last game, giving them 16 days to rest before this showdown. Quarterback Battles and Key Players Both squads deal with injury questions at the most important spot on the field. Georgia Southern quarterback Max Johnson is listed as probable to play after leaving the ODU game with a first-half injury. item.title: Red Roses cruise to dominant victory over United States in final WXV game
item.description: England Women had a much easier time against the United States after two successive defeats by Canada - Getty Images/Caean Couto United States 12 England 55 English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach. The Red Roses were in the unfamiliar position of coming off the back of successive defeats and Meg Jones had called on her team to respond. They certainly did that, looking far more like world champions than they have over the past fortnight with a convincing nine - try win – four of them scored by Claudia Moloney-MacDonald – albeit there is still room for them to “grow”, as Jones put it after the game. That is what the Rugby Football Union have been trying to do off the field. Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, and his colleagues used this fixture in New Jersey as an opportunity to tap into the US market by “creating connections” with business leaders and potential investors. It is little wonder English rugby is trying to get a piece of the American pie. There are an ever-growing number of US owners in British football and with the States hosting the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups in 2031 and 2033 interest in the oval-ball game is sure to grow too, although the crowd in New Jersey would suggest there is work to do on that front. England were back to winning ways in North America - Getty Images/Caean Couto Those potential investors at the Sports Illustrated Stadium may not have enjoyed seeing their national team so convincingly beaten, but they will surely have recognised the talent of those wearing white. England fell short of the high standards they are known for in those defeats by Canada – their first back-to-back losses in a decade – but there were marked improvements against the US. Yes, there were still a few defensive frailties and they will be disappointed by their ill-discipline at times, but their attacking play looked far slicker. In part, that was because the US did not close down the Red Roses as effectively as their Canadian counterparts, but the visitors’ handling was far sharper than it has been on this away leg of the WXV Global Series. Holly Aitchison, who replaced Zoe Harrison at fly-half in one of six changes made by John Mitchell for this Test, showed what a classy distributor she is. First came a floated pass out to Moloney-MacDonald to dive over for the opening try inside five minutes. item.title: Leclerc sets pace in Friday practice at Mexico City Grand Prix
item.description: Charles Leclerc was fastest in both practice sessions on Friday [Reuters] Ferrari's Charles Leclerc headed McLaren's Lando Norris in Friday practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who is poised to clinch his first world title on Sunday, was fourth fastest behind team-mate George Russell. Only a victory by Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can theoretically stop Antonelli becoming champion on Sunday. Even then, Antonelli only needs ninth place if Russell wins and 10th if Hamilton does. Leclerc, who topped both sessions on Friday, was 0.103 seconds quicker than Norris, with Russell just 0.003secs further adrift. Antonelli was 0.217secs off the pace, and ahead of the Red Bulls of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar. Leclerc's team-mate Lewis Hamilton was 11th overall after stopping on track with a technical problem before completing his qualifying simulation runs on the soft tyre. Behind Hadjar, Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson sandwiched Pierre Gasly's Alpine, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri completed the top 10. Verstappen and Lawson face a trip to the stewards after a collision in the stadium early in the session. The first session was marked by 10 of the 11 teams running 'rookie' drivers in their cars. One of them was Cadillac's Colton Herta, who the team are considering promoting to a race seat in place of Valtteri Bottas next season. Initially, the team felt his running in Mexico had given him enough points under the F1 system to earn a 'superlicence', which is required to race in F1. But further investigation by governing body the FIA revealed the American nine-time Indycar race winner is still one point short and will have to complete one further practice session this year to secure his licence. Aquí te contamos cómo llegan Cruz Azul y León, previo a su enfrentamiento. Cristiano Ronaldo marca Hat-Trick ante Al-Kholood ¿cuántos goles le faltan para los 1000? Los celestes llegan a este compromiso después de una semana de fecha doble perfecta, pues consiguieron 9 puntos de 9 posibles tras vencer a Juárez, Pachuca y Querétaro, estos dos últimos en condición de visitante. Además, Joel Huiqui ha optado por darle rotación a su plantel y parece tener engachada a la mayoría de la plantilla y en las últimas semanas ha recuperado a elementos importantes que estaban lesionados: Gonzalo Piovi, Carlos Rotondi y Amaury García. Por si fuera poco, Andrés Montaño ha tenido una segunda mitad de torneo de ensueño que ha hecho olvidar la ausencia de José Paradela, quien ya estará disponible para el enfrentamiento contra los panzasverdes. La Fiera se juega su boleto a la Fiesta Grande ante la máquina en la capital. To end the season, Wisconsin faces Iowa, Rutgers, Maryland, Purdue, and Minnesota. In years past, there still wouldn’t be much hope in the Badgers winning a ton of those games because of their inconsistent play. Over the past two seasons, Wisconsin has lost to Iowa and Minnesota twice each, while also losing to Maryland last season. item.description: With the offseason officially underway, the Boston Red Sox have just three days to clear enough 40-man roster spots to make room for the seven players who ended the season on the 60-day injured list. MassLive.com’s Chris Cottilo and Sean McAdam discussed this problem on the latest 'Fenway Rundown' podcast , where they suggested the former top prospect Kristian Campbell could be designated for assignment to clear the final spot on the roster. Wait… what? Once a top 10 prospect in baseball, Campbell spent the entire 2026 season in Triple-A reworking his swing. In 109 games for Worcester, the 24-year-old hit .256/.383/.380/.763 with eight home runs and 22 doubles, and driving in 51 runs while shifting to a full-time outfielder role. So you may be asking: Campbell is only 24, and he put up a good season in the minors, why would the Red Sox give up on him? Why take the risk? Sure, it seems unlikely any team would take a chance on Campbell, given that the last time he played in the big leagues, he posted a slash line of .159/.243/.222/.465 over 38 games. item.description: Oct 31, 2025; Avondale, Arizona, USA; NASCAR Truck Series drivers Grant Enfinger (9), Cole Butcher (62), Tanner Gray (15) and Tyler Ankrum (18) crash during the NASCAR Truck Series Championship race at Phoenix Raceway. The McAnally-Hilgemann Racing driver finished second in a wild four-wide sprint at Talladega Superspeedway on Friday . He pushed hard to the line, yet the math says his shot at the title is over. Per Yahoo Sports , Ankrum remains ninth in the Chase standings with 2,157 points. He now trails leader Kaden Honeycutt by 214 markers, a gap too wide to close. The runner-up spot was a bright spot in a dark afternoon for the title hunt. Ankrum started seventh and fought through the pack to finish just 0.002 seconds ahead of Austin Green. That second-place finish gave him 35 points and his seventh top-10 result of the year. It was his fourth career top-10 at this track, showing he knows how to handle the drafting lanes. But those points were not enough to keep his hopes alive. The Math Kills the Hopes Championship races in the Truck Series are often won by inches, but this one ended by points. Ankrum entered the weekend as a contender, but the gap to the front grew too large. The deficit mathematically eliminates him from title contention with just two races left. He must now look ahead to Martinsville and Homestead-Miami to build his final standing. The focus shifts from winning the title to proving he belongs in the top tier. Other drivers faced even worse luck that day. Daniel Hemric crashed out on Lap 17 after Stewart Friesen’s Toyota went unstable in Turns 1 and 2. The accident collected eight drivers and ended Hemric’s afternoon after only 16 laps. He finished 35th with just two points, leaving him seventh in the standings. The crash cost him 194 points behind Honeycutt, sealing his fate as well. Mechanical Woes and Bad Breaks It was a day where bad luck swept through the garage like a storm. Gio Ruggiero, the defending Talladega winner, led five laps and won the first stage before his truck died. His No. 17 Toyota got stuck in reverse on pit road due to a transmission problem. The field is tight, and every lap counts when the season is this far gone. Honeycutt Holds the Key While others lost ground, Kaden Honeycutt gained solid footing for the title run. This game is a major test as it will be Ohio State’s first game since Julian Sayin suffered his significant right arm injury in the Buckeyes’ October 17 victory over Indiana. "Ohio State has too many weapons outside not to be able to utilize them and that's gonna be the key in this game against USC.. It will be interesting to see how Ryan Day manages this quarterback situation" ~ Coach Saban #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/ITMtPHiPrt Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 30, 2026 Head coach Ryan Day has not announced whether Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair will be under center for the Buckeyes (6-1), but it is clear that Ohio State faces a test against the 6-2 Trojans. The Buckeyes are 6.5-point favorites against the Trojans and they appear to have multiple advantages as USC has significant defensive issues. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban says that Ryan Day needs to see his quarterbacks perform at a high enough level that the Trojans can’t put eight men in the box and just concentrate on stopping the running game. The Buckeyes have the best receiver in the country in Jeremiah Smith, and they must show they can get the ball to him and the other talented Buckeyes receivers. “Ohio State has too many weapons outside not to be able to utilize them and that’s going to be the key in this game against USC,” Saban said on the Pat McAfee Show. “It will be interesting to see how Ryan Day manages this quarterback situation” If neither Fahey nor St. Clair proves competent enough to do that, then the Buckeyes are likely in trouble in this game and those that follow. The fact that Ohio State is coming off a bye following the Sayin injury should help either quarterback get acclimated, but either signal caller will have to show that he can make the proper decisions and demonstrate the accuracy, velocity and decisiveness needed to make key plays.
